gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.intro: From install to your first screen in five minutes. One stylesheet import is the only required setup.

install.title: Installation
install.intro: Install from npm. React 18 or newer is required.

firstUse.title: First Example
firstUse.intro: The simplest possible combination of Button and Input. Labels, hints and errors are wired up even when you do not pass an id.

toastProvider.title: ToastProvider Setup
toastProvider.intro: Wrap your app root in ToastProvider to use toasts. Put DesignSystemProvider outside it so the toast region label is localized too.

theming.title: Token Customization
theming.intro: Override the --ds-* variables in your global CSS to retheme. Adjust the 600/700/800 steps together so button states keep meeting the contrast requirement.

1.question: Is it compatible with the Next.js App Router?
1.answer: Yes. The package includes the 'use client' directive so it imports directly into server components. Import the stylesheet once in your root layout.

2.question: Is dark mode supported?
2.answer: Since v0.3.1, yes. By default it follows the OS prefers-color-scheme setting, and you can force it with <html data-theme="dark"> or class="dark". Token roles are identical in both themes (neutral-0 is always the surface, neutral-900 is always the text), so components you built on tokens switch along with it.

3.question: Does tree-shaking work?
3.answer: Yes. v0.4.0 also cleaned up the forwardRef calls bundlers were mistaking for side effects, so unused components now drop out of the bundle. import { Button } measures 1.57 kB (minified + brotli).

4.question: How do I import the TypeScript types?
4.answer: Most props types are named exports, e.g. import type { ButtonProps } from 'null_ong2-design-system'. The exceptions are Box, Flex, Grid, Stack, Container and Text: they are generic over the as prop and export no props type, so derive one with ComponentProps<typeof Box>. The full list lives on the Runtime API page.

5.question: How do I change the theme colors?
5.answer: Override the --ds-color-primary-* variables under :root in your global CSS. If you also use dark mode, override the same variables in the dark selectors as well.

6.question: What happens if I forget the stylesheet import?
6.answer: Components render unstyled. In development the package checks a CSS load marker (--ds-loaded) and logs a one-time notice; in production builds it does nothing.

7.question: Can I reword the strings the components read out?
7.answer: Yes. Pass only the keys you want to change to the strings prop of DesignSystemProvider and the rest keep their locale values. For a language that is not built in, supply a full DsStrings object.

styles.title: Import the stylesheet (required)
styles.intro: Component CSS is not injected into the JS bundle. Import it once at your app entry point.
styles.note: Auto-injection was removed in v0.2.2 because it caused a flash of unstyled content under SSR (Next.js App Router and friends). Without this import components render unstyled; in development the package logs a one-time notice.

darkMode.title: Dark mode
darkMode.intro: With no configuration it follows the OS prefers-color-scheme setting. To drive it yourself, set data-theme on <html>.
darkMode.more: See the theming page for a toggle implementation and FOUC prevention →

i18n.title: Built-in string language
i18n.intro: Sets the language of labels the components produce themselves — close, loading, slide and so on. Without the provider everything stays Korean, so existing code needs no change.
i18n.more: See the i18n page for the full key list and overrides →

code.autoId: label and error stay wired up even without an id
code.followOs: With no configuration it follows the OS prefers-color-scheme.
code.controlIt: To drive it yourself, one attribute on <html>
code.providerOptional: Without the provider everything stays Korean. ko · en · ja · zh are built in.

tokens.title: Design Tokens
tokens.intro: Every CSS custom property the design system injects into :root. Override them from your global CSS to retheme.

colors.title: Colors
colors.intro: Since v0.3.1 every color token carries a light and a dark value. The left chip is light, the right chip is dark.

role.intro: Tokens named after their job rather than their value. They absorb the lightness inversion of dark mode so component CSS never has to change. In your own components, reach for these instead of neutral-0 whenever you need a foreground color on a filled surface.
role.onPrimary: Foreground on a primary surface (button text and similar).
role.controlKnob: The color laid on top of a filled control — a checkmark, a switch knob.
role.surfaceTranslucent: A translucent surface laid over content, such as the carousel arrows.
role.controlBorder: The boundary of inputs, checkboxes and switch tracks. It identifies the control, so it keeps at least 3:1 contrast against the surface.

zIndex.title: Z-index
zIndex.intro: A single ladder governs stacking. Tooltips and dropdown menus render into a body portal, so they must sit above the modal layer to avoid being clipped.

usage.dropdown: In-flow stacking such as inline dropdowns.
usage.toast: The toast container — always on top.

zIndex.caption: Z-index tokens and where they are used

shadow.title: Shadow
shadow.intro: Dark mode uses deeper values so elevation stays readable against a dark background. The preview shows the light value.

transition.title: Transition
transition.intro: How fast components move between states. When the OS "reduce motion" setting is on, component CSS overrides these and effectively removes the transitions.

borderFocus.title: Border · Focus ring
borderFocus.intro: Default borders and the keyboard focus indicator. The focus ring references an opaque color, keeping at least 3:1 contrast against the background in both themes.

internal.body: {name} is not a design token but a marker confirming the stylesheet actually loaded (value {value}). It backs the one-time development warning about a missing styles.css import, so leave it alone.

theming.title: Theming
theming.intro: Every visual value is exposed as a CSS variable. Override them in your global CSS and the theme changes immediately; dark mode comes along with no extra work.

overview.title: How it works
overview.body: Component CSS never bakes in token values at build time — it references var(--ds-*). Redefine a variable of the same name in your project and every component picks up the new value at once. Dark mode works the same way: not a line of component CSS changes, only the token values behind the selector.

example.title: Override example
example.intro: Recolor the brand to purple and soften the corners. Buttons use 600 at rest, 700 on hover and 800 on press, so adjust all three steps to keep the state changes visible.

scope.title: Scoped overrides
scope.body: Redefine the variables on a parent selector instead of :root and they apply only inside that subtree. data-theme also works on any element, not just <html>, so a single section of a page can be dark on its own.

futureBuilder.title: Live theme builder (v2)
futureBuilder.body: Picking colors with a live preview and exporting the :root CSS automatically is on the v2 roadmap. For now, copy the code block above and apply it by hand.

darkMode.title: Dark mode
darkMode.body: Token roles are identical to light — neutral-0 is always the surface, neutral-900 is always the text. Only the lightness flips, so anything that references tokens, including components you wrote, adapts on its own.
darkMode.tryIt: Try it right now with the theme buttons in this page's header. The site UI and the components in the examples below all switch from the same single data-theme attribute.

activation.title: Turning it on
activation.body: All three approaches are supported. class and data-theme behave identically, so pick whichever fits your project.

roleTokens.title: Use the role tokens
roleTokens.body: In dark mode neutral-0 is no longer white — it is the dark surface color. Using neutral-0 as text on a filled background makes that text the same color as the background. Reach for role tokens named after their job, such as --ds-color-on-primary.

overriding.title: Override both sides
overriding.body: Overriding a token under :root only changes the light value; the dark selectors are declared later, so the original dark value still wins. If you change light, change dark too.

toggle.title: Building a toggle
toggle.body: A three-way light / dark / system toggle is the practical choice. The key detail is that 'system' removes the attribute to hand control back to the OS — that is not the same as forcing light.

fouc.title: Preventing the first-paint flash
fouc.body: Waiting for React to hydrate paints one light frame before switching to dark. Read the stored choice synchronously in <head> and set the attribute first. The server HTML will differ, so <html> needs suppressHydrationWarning.

code.activationAuto: Do nothing and it follows the OS setting (prefers-color-scheme)
code.activationLight: Pin to light (stays light even when the OS is dark)
code.darkValue: Dark value — override dark wherever you overrode light
code.systemRemovesAttr: For system, remove the attribute to hand control back to the OS.
code.scopedSelector: Define them on any selector instead of :root and they apply only inside that subtree.
code.scopedAnyElement: data-theme works on any element, not just <html>
code.scopedInside: only the components in here use the dark tokens
code.roleTokenWhy: neutral-0 becomes the dark surface color in dark mode. Use a role token for foregrounds.

componentsIndex.title: Components
componentsIndex.intro: Catalog of every component grouped by category.

props.label: Screen-reader label. Omitted, it falls back to the current locale's 'Loading'.

do.1: Show it the moment async work begins so users know progress is happening.
do.2: Make the label specific (e.g. 'Loading data').

dont.1: Don't flash a spinner for sub-200ms work — it just looks broken.
dont.2: Don't leave users on a spinner forever. Time out and show an error.

spinner.a11y: Spinner reports progress through role='status' and aria-label. Its color inherits currentColor, so set it from the parent. When 'reduce motion' is on it does not stop — it slows to a 3-second rotation, keeping the in-progress signal while reducing the discomfort.

skeleton.description: Shimmering placeholder shown while content loads.

props.width: Width. Number = px, string = CSS value.

do.1: Match the dimensions of the real content to avoid layout shift.
do.2: Vary widths across multiple lines for a natural text feel.

dont.1: For sub-1s responses, prefer Spinner over Skeleton.
dont.2: Don't hardcode pixels only — use % or fr to keep responsive layouts intact.

skeleton.a11y: Skeleton is aria-hidden='true' so screen readers skip it. Replace it with the real content as it arrives.

alert.description: Inline notification banner with built-in icons for 4 variants.

props.title: Optional title.
props.icon: Custom icon. Falls back to a variant-specific default.

do.1: Tell users what to do next, especially in error alerts.
do.2: Reserve warning/danger for time-sensitive situations.

dont.1: Don't auto-dismiss Alert like a toast — Toast is the right tool there.
dont.2: More than 5 same-variant alerts on a screen and users tune them out.

alert.a11y: warning/danger get role='alert' for immediate announcement; info/success get role='status' for non-intrusive announcement. ARIA is set automatically.

avatar.description: Avatar with image and initials fallback. 5 sizes, circle or square.

props.name: The person's name, used for alt text and the initials fallback. Initials are split on grapheme boundaries, so emoji are never cut in half.

do.1: Always provide name so the initials fallback works when the image fails to load.
do.2: Use a uniform size across lists for clean alignment.

dont.1: Don't omit alt — screen readers won't convey meaning.
dont.2: Don't drop arbitrary images in without a size — they break alignment.

avatar.a11y: Avatar carries meaning through img alt or aria-label. The initials fallback has role='img' plus aria-label so the name is announced, and when neither name nor alt is given it falls back to the current locale's 'User avatar'. Changing src to a new value clears the previous failure and retries.

props.dot: Renders only a dot, with no text. Children passed alongside it are hidden visually but still announced by screen readers.
props.children: The badge content. Combined with dot it is hidden visually and left for screen readers only.

do.1: Match variant to meaning (success=done, danger=error).
do.2: Cap large counts as '99+' so the label can't break out.

dont.1: Don't make Badge clickable — Button is right for actions.
dont.2: More than 5 badges in a row dilutes attention.

badge.a11y: A Badge conveys its meaning through its text content. Even as a dot, children you pass survive as visually hidden text, so <Badge dot>3</Badge> does not silently drop the '3'.

code.dotSr: Only the dot is visible, but '3' is still announced by screen readers.

carousel.description: Shows one slide at a time, with autoplay, indicators, arrows and a play/pause control.

props.index: The current index (controlled). Values outside the slide range are clamped back to a real slide.
props.autoPlayInterval: Autoplay interval in ms. 0 disables it (default 0).
props.ariaLabel: Accessible label for the carousel region. Omitted, it falls back to the current locale's 'Carousel'.

do.1: Use autoplay intervals of at least 4 seconds so users have time to read.
do.2: Keep slides to 5 or fewer so indicators remain meaningful.

dont.1: Don't put critical info only in a carousel — slides past the first see steep drop-offs.
dont.2: Do not set autoplay below three seconds — it moves on before anyone can read it.

carousel.a11y: Identified by role='region' plus aria-roledescription='carousel'. Off-screen slides are marked inert, so they leave both the tab order and the accessibility tree entirely. Indicators follow the tablist convention (roving tabindex, arrows, Home/End) and keep a 24×24 hit area. Autoplay pauses on hover, on focus and via the stop button, and never starts at all when the OS 'reduce motion' setting is on (WCAG 2.2.2).

tabs.description: Compound tabs with arrow-key navigation, supporting horizontal and vertical orientations.

List.aria-label: Accessible label for the tab bar (tablist). Always distinguish them when a screen holds more than one tab group.

Root.defaultValue: The initially active tab. Omitted, the first Trigger is selected automatically.
Root.orientation: Orientation: 'horizontal' (default) or 'vertical'. The arrow-key mapping changes with it.
Root.children: Tabs.List and Tabs.Panel — the children that form the compound structure.

do.1: Tabs read best at 4 or fewer. Beyond that, prefer side navigation.
do.2: Keep each label to 1–2 words.

dont.1: Don't use tabs for page-level routing — tabs are for the same context.
dont.2: Don't nest tabs inside tabs.

tabs.a11y: Implements the full ARIA pattern with role=tablist/tab/tabpanel and aria-selected/aria-controls. Keyboard: left/right (up/down when vertical) wraps around, Home/End jump to the ends. Because the first tab is selected automatically even without defaultValue, the roving tabindex never collapses into a tab bar no keyboard can reach. The panel shows a focus ring when it receives focus.

modal.description: An overlay dialog. Focus trap, close on Escape, close on overlay click, background scroll lock and background assistive-technology blocking are all applied automatically.

props.title: Title (optional).
props.aria-label: Accessible name for a dialog without a title. Ignored when title is set.
props.closeOnOverlayClick: Close when the overlay is clicked (default true). It only closes when the press started on the overlay, so dragging a text selection out of the body and releasing outside will not close it.
props.initialFocusRef: The element that receives focus when the dialog opens. Omitted, focus goes to the first focusable element inside (usually the close button). Use it to land on 'Cancel' in a destructive confirmation.

do.1: Always provide a title so the user knows the dialog's purpose.
do.2: For destructive actions build the footer from secondary (Cancel) plus danger (Confirm), and point initialFocusRef at Cancel.

dont.1: Don't nest modals — users get lost.
dont.2: Don't use modals for one-off info; a page or a toast is often enough.

modal.a11y: Carries role='dialog' with aria-modal='true' and traps keyboard focus inside the dialog. A focus trap only blocks Tab, so the background also gets aria-hidden and inert to stop screen-reader rotor and swipe navigation (the toast container is excluded). Background scroll is locked with position: fixed so it works on iOS Safari too, and the scroll position is restored on close. When dialogs are stacked, Escape only reaches the topmost one.

code.longScroll: A long body scrolls inside the dialog.

tooltip.description: A small overlay with supporting text on hover or focus. It renders into a body portal so an overflow ancestor cannot clip it.

props.children: The trigger element (required, a single React element). Passing a string or multiple elements raises an error that tells you exactly what to fix.
props.disabled: Disables the tooltip (default false). Flipping it to true while open closes the tooltip immediately.

do.1: Reserve Tooltip for supplementary info — critical info must always be visible.
do.2: Short text like keyboard shortcuts or icon meanings is the sweet spot.

dont.1: Don't put interactive elements (buttons, links) inside Tooltip — they're not keyboard reachable.
dont.2: Don't hide critical info that's only available on hover; touch users can't access it.

tooltip.a11y: floating-ui's role hook wires the trigger's aria-describedby and the tooltip's id to the same value, so screen readers read the description. It also appears on keyboard focus and closes on Escape. Inside clipping ancestors such as a modal body or a carousel viewport, the body portal plus a fixed strategy keeps it fully visible.

dropdownMenu.description: A click-triggered dropdown menu. Keyboard behavior follows the WAI-ARIA APG menu pattern, and it renders into a body portal.

props.trigger: The trigger element (required, a single React element).

do.1: Mark destructive actions with destructive: true for a clear visual cue.
do.2: Group items visually when there are 5+ entries.

dont.1: Don't put form inputs inside DropdownMenu — menus are for actions.
dont.2: If the trigger is icon-only, always provide aria-label.

dropdownMenu.a11y: Uses role='menu' and role='menuitem'. Opening from the trigger with up/down or Enter/Space moves focus to the first (or last) item; up/down wraps and skips disabled items. Escape or an outside click closes it and returns focus to the trigger. Arrow keys never land on a stale item after the list shrinks. It renders into a body portal so overflow ancestors cannot clip it.

toast.description: Global notification system. Wrap your app root in ToastProvider, then call useToast.

ToastProvider.maxToasts: Maximum number shown at once (default 5). Values of 0 or less are clamped up to 1.
ToastProvider.children: The app tree the provider wraps. Toasts themselves render into a portal outside this tree.

do.1: Keep toasts to a single concise line.
do.2: Scale duration with message length — longer messages need 5–7s.

dont.1: Don't surface form-validation errors via toast — show them next to the input.
dont.2: Do not show more than five toasts at once — cap it with maxToasts.

toast.a11y: The toast container stays mounted with role='region' and aria-live='polite' even when empty — a live region has to exist before its content for a screen reader to announce changes. warning and danger additionally escalate to role='alert' because they need immediate attention. Hovering or focusing the container pauses the auto-dismiss timer, and leaving resumes from the time that was left (WCAG 2.2.1).

text.description: Body text component supporting size, weight, and color tokens.

props.truncate: When true, truncates to one line with ellipsis.

do.1: Use semantic color names so meaning carries through (danger = error).
do.2: For long body, lean on the default size + line-height — they're already readable.

dont.1: Don't use Text size='4xl' for a heading — semantics differ. Use Heading.
dont.2: Don't pass arbitrary hex to color — semantic tokens first.

text.a11y: Text renders as p by default, so screen readers treat it as a paragraph. When using as="span" inline, you may need extra ARIA to convey meaning.

heading.description: Section heading component. Set the semantic level (as) and the visual size (size) independently.

props.size: Visual font size. Auto-derived from level when omitted.
props.color: Text color (CSS variable or color value).

do.1: Use exactly one as='h1' for the top-level page title.
do.2: If a small visual is needed, use as='h2' size='sm' — keep semantics intact.

dont.1: Don't skip heading levels for styling (no h1 → h3 directly).
dont.2: Don't reuse h2 for every search-result item — handle it visually only.

heading.a11y: Heading renders as semantic h1–h6 elements that screen readers use for landmark navigation. Keep the order so users can scan the page quickly.

label.description: Label associated with a form input.

props.required: Show required marker. When true, adds a red asterisk.

do.1: Match htmlFor to the input id exactly so clicking the label focuses it.
do.2: Just use the label prop on Input/Textarea/Select — no need for a separate Label.

dont.1: Don't float Label as an in-input placeholder — it disappears on focus and breaks accessibility.
dont.2: Don't use placeholder alone without a label — screen readers lose meaning.

label.a11y: Label is explicitly linked to its input via htmlFor, so click moves focus and screen readers announce the field name.

box.description: General-purpose layout container. A polymorphic component whose rendered element you can change via the as prop.

props.as: HTML element or component to render. Defaults to div.
props.padding: Padding on all sides. Accepts SpacingKey (0–16, xs–2xl).
props.bg: Background color. Accepts CSS variable or raw color value.

do.1: Use design tokens (SpacingKey, RadiusKey) for consistency.
do.2: Make use of the as prop to render semantic elements (section, article).

dont.1: Don't pass arbitrary px/% to padding/margin. Use the tokens.
dont.2: Don't shoehorn every layout into Box — pick Flex/Stack/Grid where they fit better.

box.a11y: Box renders a div by default and carries no semantics. For meaningful regions, set as="section" or as="article" appropriately.

flex.description: Flexbox layout component. Polymorphic with gap-token support.

do.1: Use Flex when alignment is meaningful. For pure stacking, Stack reads better.
do.2: Prefer gap tokens over child margins.

dont.1: Don't compute child widths with precise percentages — that defeats Flex's value.
dont.2: For complex 2D layouts, Grid is correct.

flex.a11y: Flex renders a div, so set semantics via as. If horizontal scrolling appears, consider overflow: auto for keyboard users.

stack.description: Stacks children at a consistent gap. The most-used layout component.

do.1: Reach for Stack first for linear stacking — clearer than Flex.
do.2: Use spacing tokens for a consistent rhythm.

dont.1: If you need space-between alignment, Flex justify="space-between" is clearer than Stack.
dont.2: Mixed vertical+horizontal layouts are usually better as Grid than nested Stacks.

stack.a11y: Stack renders a div. Add semantics via as="ul" or as="section" when meaningful.

grid.description: CSS Grid layout. Pass a number to columns for equal columns, or a string for direct grid-template-columns.

props.columns: Number of columns or grid-template-columns string.
props.rows: Number of rows or grid-template-rows string.

do.1: For uniform card lists, pass a number to columns.
do.2: For responsive cards, use 'repeat(auto-fill, minmax(...))'.

dont.1: Don't use Grid for unidirectional stacks — Stack is lighter and clearer.
dont.2: Don't pass arbitrary px values into minmax — use tokens or meaningful ratios.

grid.a11y: Grid is purely visual. Convey meaning with semantic children (article, li, etc.).

container.description: Constrains content to a max width and centers it. Pick a width via the maxWidth prop (sm–2xl).

props.maxWidth: Max width. sm 640px / md 768px / lg 1024px / xl 1280px / 2xl 1536px / full 100%.

do.1: Use maxWidth="sm" or "md" for long-form text to keep line length readable.
do.2: Set as="main" so the page's main content is semantically marked.

dont.1: Don't use Container for full-bleed regions like headers/footers.
dont.2: Don't nest multiple Containers — one Container per page is the norm.

container.a11y: Container has no semantics by itself. Use as="main" / as="article" / etc. matching the page structure.

input.description: A text input with built-in support for label, hint, and error message.

props.id: The input's id. Omitted, a unique id is generated internally to connect the label, hint and error.
props.label: Label text. When provided, the Label component is rendered automatically.
props.hint: Hint message shown beneath the input when no error is present.
props.error: Error message. When non-empty the field turns red and the message is announced with role='alert'.
props.required: Whether the field is required. Adds a red asterisk to the label.
props.type: HTML input type — supports email, password, number, etc.
props.placeholder: Placeholder text shown when the value is empty.

do.1: Write specific error messages like 'Must be at least 8 characters', not 'Invalid'.
do.2: The label prop wires the association for you. Never let a placeholder stand in for a label.

dont.1: Avoid abstract error messages like 'Error occurred' — users won't know what to fix.
dont.2: Don't mark required fields with only an asterisk. Set the required prop too.

input.a11y: The label and input are connected by id so screen readers announce the field name. Even without an id the internal unique id keeps the association, so several fields side by side never collide. In the error state aria-invalid='true' is applied and the error and hint are linked through aria-describedby — and an aria-describedby you pass yourself is merged in rather than overwritten.

textarea.description: Multi-line text input following the same label/hint/error pattern as Input.

props.id: The textarea's id. Omitted, a unique id is generated internally to connect the label, hint and error.
props.label: Label text.

do.1: For long input, set rows large enough to give visible breathing room.
do.2: If there's a character limit, surface it in the hint, e.g. 'Up to 500 characters'.

dont.1: Don't use Textarea for short single-line input — Input is correct there.
dont.2: Don't force resize: none — let users adjust the height.

textarea.a11y: Follows the same conventions as Input — generated id, aria-invalid on error, aria-describedby for the error and hint, and merging with an aria-describedby you pass. resize: vertical is the default, so the size is adjustable from the keyboard alone.

checkbox.description: Checkbox supporting both controlled and uncontrolled usage.

props.id: The checkbox's id. The label stays explicitly connected even if you omit it.
props.label: Label rendered next to the checkbox.
props.onChange: Change handler. Receives boolean as the first argument.

do.1: Always pair a checkbox with a clear label.
do.2: Group related checkboxes using fieldset/legend to express the relationship.

dont.1: Use Switch for binary ON/OFF settings; Checkbox is for multi-select.
dont.2: Don't disable required-agreement checkboxes — surface an error instead.

checkbox.a11y: Renders a semantic input[type=checkbox] toggled with Space. Even without an id the internal unique id links it to the label, so clicking the label always works.

radio.description: Radio button — only one radio in the same name group can be selected.

props.id: The radio's id. The label stays explicitly connected even if you omit it.
props.name: Group name. Radios in the same group share this name.
props.value: Value passed to onChange when selected.
props.label: Label rendered next to the radio.
props.onChange: Change handler. Receives the string value as the first argument.

do.1: Prefer Radio over Select when there are 5 or fewer options.
do.2: Give all radios in a group the exact same name.

dont.1: If there are exactly 2 toggle-style options, use Switch instead of Radio.
dont.2: Don't leave a non-required radio group entirely unselected — provide a default.

radio.a11y: Renders input[type=radio], so arrow keys move within the group. Even without an id the internal unique id links it to the label.

select.description: Dropdown select. Options are passed via the options prop.

props.id: The select's id. Omitted, a unique id is generated internally to connect the label, hint and error.
props.label: Label text.
props.options: Array of options. SelectOption[] with value/label/disabled.
props.placeholder: Text for the leading guidance option. With no value or defaultValue, that option is the initial selection.

do.1: Use Select when there are 6 or more options. For fewer, Radio reads better.
do.2: Use a placeholder only when there is no obvious default. Passing one makes the guidance text appear first without needing a separate defaultValue.

dont.1: Don't use code-only abbreviations as labels — use names users understand.
dont.2: Don't show a placeholder for a required field but skip the required prop.

select.a11y: Built on the native select element, so platform accessibility and mobile UX come for free. The label is connected even without an id, and in the error state aria-invalid and aria-describedby are applied automatically and merged with any aria-describedby you pass.

switch.description: Instant ON/OFF toggle. Use it for settings that take effect immediately, unlike Checkbox.

props.id: The switch's id. The label stays explicitly connected even if you omit it.
props.label: Label rendered next to the toggle.
props.size: Toggle size. sm 28×16, md 36×20, lg 44×24 pixels.
props.onChange: Change handler. Receives boolean as the first argument.

do.1: Use Switch for instantly applied ON/OFF. For form-submit settings, Checkbox is correct.
do.2: Label the switch by what's enabled when ON, e.g. 'Enable notifications'.

dont.1: Don't add 'On/Off' helper text — the visual state already conveys it.
dont.2: If the user batches several toggles before applying, Checkbox + Apply button is the right pattern.

switch.a11y: Renders input[role=switch] so screen readers recognize it as a toggle. Space toggles it and aria-checked reports the state. The label is connected even without an id.

button.description: A button that triggers a user action. Supports 4 variants, 3 sizes, plus loading, disabled, and icon states.

props.variant: Visual style. Use 'primary' for the most prominent action.
props.isLoading: When true a spinner is shown and clicks are disabled. aria-busy and aria-disabled are applied automatically.
props.disabled: When true, the button is visually and functionally disabled.
props.leftIcon: Icon node rendered to the left of the label. Accepts any ReactNode.
props.rightIcon: Icon node rendered to the right of the label.

do.1: Use action verbs as labels ('Save', 'Delete') so users know exactly what happens.
do.2: Wrap destructive actions (deletion) in the danger variant for a clear visual cue.

dont.1: Avoid multiple primary buttons on the same page or section — they compete for attention.
dont.2: Don't pass both isLoading and disabled together. isLoading already disables interaction.

button.a11y: Renders a semantic <button> operated with Enter/Space. While isLoading, aria-busy='true' and aria-disabled='true' are applied. Becoming disabled makes the browser throw focus back to body, which loses a keyboard user's place — so when loading finishes the button takes focus back, but only if nothing else claimed it in the meantime. Add an aria-label for icon-only buttons.

i18n.title: Localization
i18n.intro: Sets the language of the strings components read out on their own. ko (default), en, ja and zh are built in, and any key can be overridden.

why.title: Why it matters
why.body: Some labels are produced by the components themselves — the modal's close button, the spinner's loading state, the carousel's next slide. Most are never painted on screen and only reach screen readers, which makes the problem invisible to the eye, but a hard-coded Korean label is a wall for everyone who does not read Korean.

setup.title: Setup
setup.intro: Wrap your app root in DesignSystemProvider and pass a locale.
setup.optional: It is optional. Without the provider everything falls back to Korean, so existing code keeps working unchanged.
setup.localeList: The list of supported locales and the default are exported as constants too. Iterate them instead of hard-coding a list when you build a language picker.

next.title: Next.js App Router
next.intro: The provider is a client component, so keep it in its own file and use it from the layout. ToastProvider reads its region label from the built-in strings, so DesignSystemProvider has to sit outside it.

strings.title: String keys
strings.intro: The table below is not transcribed into these docs — it reads the values the package actually exports. Placeholders in braces such as {index} are substituted at render time.
strings.caption: Built-in string keys and their value per locale

override.title: Overriding strings
override.intro: Pass only the keys you want to change to the strings prop; the rest keep their locale values.

customLocale.title: Languages that are not built in
customLocale.body: To use a language the locale prop does not cover, pass a complete DsStrings object as strings. Spread the closest built-in locale first and change only the keys you need, so nothing is left out.

consumer.title: Using them in your own components
consumer.intro: useDsStrings and useDsFormat read the same strings directly. Without a provider they return the default locale, so they are safe to call anywhere.

caveats.title: Things to know
caveats.noAutoDetect: The browser language is never auto-detected. Server and client would disagree and produce an SSR hydration mismatch, so locale must always be passed explicitly.
caveats.defaultKo: The default locale is 'ko'. That choice preserves the previous behavior; pass locale="en" if you want English as your baseline.
caveats.contentStrings: These strings only cover the components' built-in labels. Content you pass in — button text, modal titles — belongs to your own i18n tooling.

code.englishStrings: every component inside here uses the English built-in strings
code.toastOutside: ToastProvider reads its region label from the built-in strings, so keep it inside.
code.buildPicker: Build the language picker straight from the built-in locale list.
code.onlyGivenKeys: Only the keys you name are replaced; the rest keep their locale values.
code.fillAllKeys: For a language that is not built in, pass every key.

runtimeApi.title: Runtime API
runtimeApi.intro: Everything the package exports besides components — six hooks, sixteen value-list constants, the token constants and the shared types.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.intro: The reusable parts of the components' internals, made public. Building an overlay the design system does not ship? These give you the same behavior Modal has. They are all client hooks, so in the Next.js App Router use them from a file marked 'use client'.

useBodyScrollLock.description: Locks <body> scrolling while active. iOS Safari ignores overflow: hidden, so it uses position: fixed and restores the scroll position on release.

useControllable.description: Handles controlled and uncontrolled in one place. If the mode flips mid-life (value moving between a value and undefined) it warns in development.

useEscapeKey.description: Adds close-on-Escape. An internal stack makes sure only the most recently activated overlay responds when several are open.

useFocusTrap.description: Traps focus inside a container. On activation it moves to initialFocus (or the first focusable element); on deactivation it restores the previously focused element.

useInertBackground.description: Hides background content from assistive technology. A focus trap only blocks Tab, so this is what stops screen-reader rotor and swipe navigation from reaching the background.

usePrefersReducedMotion.description: Reads the OS 'reduce motion' setting. Anything that moves on its own — autoplay, auto-rotation — must stop when this is true (WCAG 2.2.2).

constants.title: Value-list constants
constants.intro: A type alone cannot be iterated at runtime, so there is no way to ask 'what values are allowed'. Use these to build a variant picker or to validate a string that arrived from a server. The table below is itself built by iterating them.
constants.caption: Value-list constants and their values

tokenConstants.title: Token constants
tokenConstants.intro: Reference the design tokens from TypeScript. The values are CSS variable references rather than hard-coded colors, so overriding the theme also moves everything that uses them.

types.title: Shared types
types.intro: The 38 types the package exports. Most component props types are exposed, but there are exceptions, so the full list is below.

noProps.title: Components without an exported props type
noProps.body: Box, Flex, Grid, Stack, Container and Text are generic over the as prop, so they do not export a props type. Derive one with React utilities when you need the type for the default element.

polymorphic.title: Building polymorphic components
polymorphic.body: PolymorphicProps lets you build your own as-prop component on exactly the same conventions as the design system.

code.scrollLockRefCount: Stacked overlays lock once via a reference count; the last one to close restores it.
code.controllableMode: Pass value for controlled; omit it and the hook keeps state internally.
code.escapeTopmost: Only the most recently activated overlay in the stack responds.
code.focusTrapInitial: Focus lands on Cancel when it opens, and returns to the previous element on close.
code.inertWhy: A focus trap only blocks Tab. This is what also stops rotor and swipe navigation.
code.inertLayers: Overlay layers marked with data-ds-layer, such as the toast container, are left alone.
code.reducedMotionSsr: Returns false under SSR and anywhere matchMedia is unavailable.
code.constantsPicker: Build a variant picker straight from the value list
code.constantsValidate: Validate at runtime that a string from the server is an allowed value
code.tokenConstantsNote: The values are CSS variable references, so overriding the theme moves these too.
code.typesNote: Build a component that supports the as prop exactly like the design system does.
code.polymorphicNoProps: these six do not export a props type — derive it with React utilities
